summary: Stale embedding cache due to namespace TTL causing incorrect rerank ordering and elevated tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed out-of-order rerank results and intermittent increases in tail latency for their reranking API (embeddings -> rerank) starting 2026-03-10 08:17 UTC. Problem localized to a single embedding namespace used by NoteAble Analytics.

Impact:
- Incorrect top-k ordering for search results (customers report relevant item ranked lower).
- Elevated p95/p99 latency for rerank calls (spikes up to 2.5s vs normal ~300ms).
- Affects production traffic only for customer NoteAble Analytics (enterprise).

Environment:
- prod/us-east region
- embedding namespace: noteable-prod-v1
- embedding cache service: redis-backed in-memory shard with per-namespace TTL override feature
- affected routes: /v1/embeddings/stream -> /v1/rerank

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Upload batch of embeddings into namespace noteable-prod-v1 with TTL unset (relies on default).
2) Issue a rerank request that depends on the cached prefix embeddings.
3) Observe rerank order mismatches and tail latency spikes during a cache refresh window.

Observed behavior:
- Cache entries for the customer's namespace sometimes persisted beyond intended TTL leading to stale vectors being served for a period after upstream re-ingest.
- When the cache served stale entries, the reranker performed extra fallback fetches, causing queueing and cascading latency (p95/p99 rise).
- Metrics show increased cache-hit churn and bursts of backend read-throughs to object store.

Expected behavior:
- Namespace-level TTL honored; re-ingested embeddings should replace stale cache entries within the TTL window and not produce prolonged stale hits.
- No tail-latency regression during cache refreshes.

Logs / Links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/namespace-noteable-prod-v1
- Support Slack thread: #support-noteable-786451 (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02ABCD123)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ingest embeddings into namespace noteable-prod-v1. 2) Wait for scheduled re-ingest that updates vector payloads. 3) Immediately send rerank requests using previously cached ids. 4) Observe rerank ordering mismatches and latency spikes in grafana.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC - Support triaged and escalated to SRE after customer provided sample request/response with out-of-order top-k.
2026-03-10 10:12 UTC - SRE confirmed spikes in redis read-throughs correlated with re-ingest windows (see grafana panel).
Hypothesis A: namespace TTL override not applied consistently due to race in the cache invalidation path during bulk re-ingest.
Hypothesis B: cache shard sticky routing caused stale replica to be read until background repair ran (possible replication lag).
Cache logs show occasional "stale-serve" events where cached vector-version < latest-version for given id; occurred 0.6% of requests for this namespace between 08:00-10:00 UTC.
Reproducer: running a bulk re-ingest of 50k embeddings with immediate rerank load produced similar behavior in staging using the same TTL configuration.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround (2026-03-10 12:45 UTC): Forced namespace cache flush for noteable-prod-v1 and temporarily increased cache write-through consistency (sync writes) to avoid read-before-write races.

Medium-term fix (deployed 2026-03-12): Patch applied to cache invalidation path to atomically update version tags on write and to honor per-namespace TTL on re-ingest. Change included additional replication sanity checks to avoid serving from lagging replica shards.
PRs: infra#4221 and serving#389 merged and rolled out to prod/us-east with canary first, then 100%.
Post-deploy validation: p95/p99 latency returned to baseline; rerank ordering matches ground-truth set provided by customer on validation run (2026-03-12 17:30 UTC).
Follow-ups: Add unit/integration tests around atomic version tag updates and add alerting for "stale-serve" rate > 0.1% per namespace. Owner: Marcus Li.
